newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lloyds plans dissolving agreement with Brazil bank.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds plans dissolving agreement with Brazil bank.

text.p: Lloyds Bank in Brazil said it plans to dissolve a 19-year-old partnership with local bank Banco Multiplic, but noted talks between the two groups have just begun and no agreement has been set yet.

"We inform that there is an intention of the shareholders of Banco Multiplic, Lloyds Bank in Brazil and Multiplic Empreendimentos to dissolve a 19-year-old partnership between the two institutions," it said in a statement.
However, the negotiations have just begun and nothing has been formalized yet, the statement added.

Lloyds Bank's statement followed press reports on Tuesday saying that the bank was about to announce the purchase of Banco Multiplic's assets. Lloyds Bank owns 50 percent of Multiplic's shares, while holding company Multiplic Empreendimentos, controlled by Brazilian bankers Ronaldo Cesar Coelho and Antonio Jose Carneiro, owns the remainder, the reports said.
Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said Lloyds Bank was only awaiting the Bank of England to approve the deal, estimated at $600 million.
Banco Multiplic is a private bank focusing mostly on capital markets.
